svg.text: Continuous query (Fig 14-1)
SQL declares the result; the engine does the work; runs forever on
each arriving event (a relational query ends when its bounded data
ends); example: filter out events with value 5 or less; no ANSI
standard, so syntax differs by framework (Flink SQL, Spark SQL)
Streams become tables
upsert table: needs a primary key, new overwrites old (a
materialisation); append-only: keeps every record, no key;
retraction: whole row is the key, +I and +D events; check your
framework supports at least append-only and upsert
Enrichment example (Flink SQL)
tables over Photographs (JSON) and Photographers (Avro with the
Confluent schema registry); metadata catalogue (Hive or JDBC);
INNER JOIN on photographer_id into Enriched_Photographs; tombstones
on either source delete the joined row; primary key NOT ENFORCED
Ways to execute
CLI (testing and local development; the job ends when it exits);
embedded in an application (fits pipelines, testing, scaling);
notebooks (Zeppelin, Jupyter) for exploration; SQL gateway
(Fig 14-2) for simple stable queries such as joiners
Notebooks: interactive cells, documentation, shareable, multi-language; but poor version control (nbdime, Jupytext help), limited scale, testing and promotion:
use for exploration, then port to a dedicated microservice.
SQL sidecar (Fig 14-3): a SQL job does joins and aggregations and writes a private stream (Private_Stream_F2AZ) for a microservice in the same bounded context;
terminate the job with the service (no zombies).
UDFs (Flink, Spark): one-to-one, many-to-one aggregates, one-to-many; can call external systems or GenAI models.
